dialogues.speaker: Marat
dialogues.text: My dear friend, there is nothing wrong with your performance. If anything, the scene itself has drifted away from the feeling the author was trying to create. I would revise it like this...

dialogues.speaker: Marat
dialogues.text: "The ghosts close their hands around the faithless man's throat and drag him toward death. Then, at that very moment, the woman he betrayed appears before him — sword in hand."

dialogues.speaker: Leanid
dialogues.text: Ah, now that is a clever turn... Before, all the woman could do was weep and mourn. Her love felt too delicate, too helpless. But now? Now she stands like a warrior. So, has she come to save the very man who betrayed her?

dialogues.speaker: Leanid
dialogues.text: "'Even if you do not love me, I still love you.' The woman raises her sword high. This is her vow and her declaration of war against the vengeful ghosts."

dialogues.speaker: Leanid
dialogues.text: Ah, now that is love in its purest form! My dear friend, I'll make sure the playwright hears your idea.

dialogues.speaker: Leanid
dialogues.text: And I, the faithless man she comes to save, will be moved by the sincerity of her heart. Her love will give me the strength to tear myself free from the ghosts' clutches, and become, at long last, a man who can shoulder his responsibilities.

dialogues.speaker: Marat
dialogues.text: Hmm... Yes, that is moving. But perhaps there is an even finer way to play it.

dialogues.speaker: Marat
dialogues.text: "The woman raises her sword high. The faithless man believes she has come to grant him salvation. Hope and gratitude begin to shine in his eyes."

dialogues.speaker: Marat
dialogues.text: "'My dear,' he says, 'I can feel your love at last.' The woman smiles beautifully, as if she has only just discovered what love tastes like."

dialogues.speaker: Marat
dialogues.text: "And then, by her own hand, she kills him. Her revenge was never something she needed to leave to the ghosts."

dialogues.speaker: Leanid
dialogues.text: Hmm... I'll have to think that one over. After all, my dear friend, I am the one playing the faithless man here. With every new idea, his fate grows a little more tragic.

dialogues.speaker: Marat
dialogues.text: Haha, no need to get that deep into character... The more tragic he is, the more sympathy he'll get. With a storyline like that, people will remember your name in no time!
